tasks.short: Coordinate HR and reward staff, set priorities, supervise delivery, and resolve escalations.

steps.what: Review open cases, deadlines, and planned reward activities.
Combine workload, availability, and dependencies into the team capacity sheet.
Choose priorities and proposed assignments against deadlines and staff capability.
Discuss assignments, coach staff, and agree responses to sensitive cases.
Write the agreed action list with owners and deadlines.
Approve and send staff instructions.
Review delivery and resolve exceptions requiring management judgement.

tasks.design: Configure a workload view in the {PROJECT}, with permitted case metadata from the {HCM} and a deterministic capacity calculation on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Structured decision notes generate an action plan for approval in the {WORKFLOW}, which updates the {PROJECT} and sends instructions through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Workload and availability were held separately. Small integrations competed with larger projects, while sensitive supervision still needed personal attention.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reporting and approval features handle much of the work. AI-assisted coding makes the remaining adapters and templates cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Case complexity is difficult to estimate. Coaching, conflicts, and employee relations require context that workload counts cannot capture.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising overload, developing staff, and deciding when a sensitive case needs a different owner or approach.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting status to coaching and resolving difficult cases. Existing assignment authority remains; no new employment decision rights arise automatically.

reach.task: Coordinate capacity across recruitment, employee relations, and reward.
reach.learn: Understand competing service deadlines and which case details can be shared.

reach.task: Coordinate reward changes with payroll cutoffs.
reach.learn: Learn payroll validation windows, correction routes, and handoff requirements.

evidence.claim: Structured workload aggregation, templates, and approval routing can use deterministic software; effort estimates remain unvalidated.
A Danish study covering 11 occupations including HR found 2.8% hours saved; it does not establish savings for this task.
GDPR Article 22 limits solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on employees.

assumptions: A mid-size employer has a small reward team within a broader HR function.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates; coordination remains the largest component.
Decision notes use structured owner, action, and deadline fields, so no model loop is needed.
Capacity calculations use working availability without exposing absence reasons.
Build ranges cover active working days for one team; national rules may require consultation and longer elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether the {HCM} and {PROJECT} expose permitted interfaces or exports.
Whether case records and staff availability are current enough for planning.
Which assignment changes require additional approval or employee consultation.
Whether national rules require consultation about the proposed workload view.
research_questions: Which workload measures predict delays without becoming individual performance scores?
Can existing reporting and approval features remove the need for custom code?
new_work: Correct stale workload and availability records.
Review generated staff instructions before sending.
Handle missing owners, conflicting deadlines, and integration failures.
Maintain capacity assumptions and access permissions.

tasks.short: Prepare job descriptions, job families, and levels with managers and agree their classification.

steps.what: Gather existing role records, descriptions, and evaluation criteria.
Interview the line manager about responsibilities, scope, and required capability.
Draft the description using the standard role template.

loop.input: Approved role evidence, interview notes, and the role template.
loop.output: A job description draft with evidence references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check required fields and evidence references; a manager verifies duties and removes unsupported statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per role; unresolved facts return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text accounts of responsibilities need synthesis; fixed templates cannot supply the substantive wording.

steps.what: Assess evaluation factors and propose the job family and level.
Calibrate proposed levels across comparable roles with managers.
Consult employee representatives on classification-system changes where required.
Approve the description and classification after required consultation.
Publish approved descriptions and update the role catalogue.

tasks.design: Keep versioned role records and evaluation criteria in the {HCM} and {DOCS}, with a structured evaluation form in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded model loop drafts descriptions from cited evidence, while deterministic checks assemble comparison packs and route approved catalogue changes to the {HCM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Role information was inconsistent, and evaluation rationales lived in separate documents. Drafting help did not resolve disagreements about actual responsibility or level.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded text drafting can work within a fixed template and evidence pack. Records, validation, comparisons, and approval routing are established software patterns.
tasks.still_hard: Managers may describe intended rather than actual work. Evaluation fairness, collective agreements, appeals, and cross-family comparisons still require skilled judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing responsibility from status, challenging inflated descriptions, and defending consistent evaluations.

ambition.what: Manager job-design clinic before a role is opened

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time on job design and contested classifications, with less document preparation. Final classification and pay authority remain with the designated approvers.

reach.role: compensation, benefits, and job analysis specialist
reach.task: Evaluate roles against a common factor framework.
reach.learn: Learn factor interpretation, calibration methods, and evidence standards.

reach.task: Prepare vacancy requirements from approved role descriptions.
reach.learn: Learn how role requirements translate into fair selection criteria.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 records job schemes for pay transparency; this supports structured records, not autonomous classification.
A UK university pilot evaluated 50 job descriptions with above 70% expert agreement; this is limited pilot evidence.
GDPR Article 22 is relevant when classification produces legally or similarly significant employee effects.
Dutch national rules include consent requirements for pay or job-evaluation systems, subject to stated exceptions.
Evidence-linked drafting and deterministic comparison packs are feasible; proposed time reductions require local validation.

assumptions: The employer has an evaluation framework or will agree one before implementation.
The time split describes a role-design change cycle; routine description updates may omit consultation.
The design uses no model-generated level recommendation or automatic employee pay change.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply; intended use determines the relevant AI obligations.
Consultation follows national rules and applicable collective agreements.
Build ranges cover active working days for one framework; consultation elapsed time can be longer.
unknowns: Which job families, evaluation factors, and reference roles are approved.
Whether the {HCM} supports versioned classification records.
Whether descriptions accurately reflect current responsibilities.
Which changes need representative consent, consultation, or an appeal route.
Who can approve classifications and any resulting pay changes.
research_questions: How accurately can bounded drafting preserve responsibility and scope without inventing duties?
Which evaluation factors produce the greatest disagreement during calibration?
Which intended uses would bring the proposed model features within AI Act high-risk requirements?
new_work: Review drafts and verify evidence references.
Resolve missing or contradictory role information.
Maintain templates, reference roles, and evaluation criteria.
Monitor description quality and biased wording.
Maintain version history and classification appeal records.

tasks.short: Identify weaknesses in HR and reward processes, develop improvements, and recommend changes to management.

steps.what: Gather process volumes, delays, errors, and benefit uptake.
Read case comments and staff feedback to identify recurring difficulties.

loop.input: Minimised case comments and staff feedback from the selected process.
loop.output: An issue summary with themes, record references, and uncertain classifications.
loop.check: Verify record references and sample each theme; separate counts from interpretation and restrict sensitive details.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one repair pass per batch; uncertain or sensitive cases go to a specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Staff describe similar difficulties in varied free text that fixed tags cannot reliably capture.

steps.what: Diagnose causes with process owners and distinguish policy problems from execution failures.
Calculate costs, workload, and employee effects for alternative changes.
Write the recommendation, supporting evidence, risks, and pilot measures.

loop.input: Reviewed problem definition, computed scenarios, and the manager's chosen recommendation outline.
loop.output: A recommendation draft with evidence references, assumptions, and pilot measures.
loop.check: Match numbers to scenario outputs; verify citations and have the manager review reasoning and tradeoffs.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unsupported causal claims return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: The narrative must connect case evidence, tradeoffs, and a chosen intervention; a fixed report only supplies tables.

steps.what: Challenge the recommendation and approve a pilot within delegated limits.
Assign pilot actions, dates, and measurement responsibilities.
Assess pilot results and recommend continuation, revision, or closure.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles permitted data from the {HCM}, {PAYROLL}, and {HELPDESK} into process measures and deterministic scenarios shown in the {BI}. Bounded loops summarise feedback and draft an evidence-linked recommendation in the {DOCS}; an approved pilot mandate creates actions in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable process measures were missing, and evidence collection was expensive. A report alone could not identify causes or secure agreement on a change.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable data adapters and scenario calculations are cheaper to build. Small text loops can organise feedback without selecting the policy response.
tasks.still_hard: Uptake and delays can reflect workforce composition or local conditions. Causal evaluation, employee trust, and consultation remain demanding.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the problem worth solving, testing explanations with employees, and balancing cost against access and fairness.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling evidence and more time testing improvements with process owners. Delegated authority to approve small pilots could shorten the cycle; it requires an explicit management mandate.

reach.task: Analyse repeat benefit enquiries and service failures.
reach.learn: Learn case taxonomy, denominator selection, and how to distinguish demand from dissatisfaction.

reach.task: Assess whether a process change creates unequal access.
reach.learn: Learn lawful comparison methods, accessibility barriers, and limits of small-group analysis.

evidence.claim: Metrics, scenario calculations, and pilot routing can be deterministic; feedback synthesis needs bounded text processing.
The digest reports a fall in HR service NPS during an HR service transformation, supporting careful service evaluation.
The AI Act lists specified employment uses as high-risk; classification depends on the system's intended use.
Dutch national rules cover specified changes involving employment, appraisal, employee data, and monitoring.

assumptions: The first build covers one process, such as benefit enrolment, rather than the whole HR function.
Time estimates include substantial diagnosis and management discussion despite automatable preparation.
The analysis uses aggregate measures and minimised text; individual performance scoring is excluded from the proposed design.
Special-category information is removed unless its processing is necessary and lawfully authorised.
Required consultation precedes pilot implementation under national rules.
Build ranges are active working days; observation of pilot outcomes adds elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether case volumes, enrolments, and error measures use consistent definitions.
Whether the employer may lawfully reuse staff feedback for this analysis.
Whether sufficient history exists to compare pilot outcomes.
Which process owners can approve operational changes.
Whether pilot approval can be delegated to the compensation and benefits manager.
research_questions: Which measures distinguish an access barrier from an employee's informed choice?
What comparison design can test the intervention without withholding employee entitlements?
How reliably do feedback themes survive removal of identifying details?
new_work: Review feedback classifications and unresolved cases.
Maintain metric definitions and cost assumptions.
Check scenario calculations against source totals.
Track pilot outcomes and unintended effects.
Maintain data connections, access controls, and retention settings.

tasks.short: Develop HR and reward policies and programmes with operational owners, legal advisers, and employee representatives.

steps.what: Collect current policies, agreements, programme rules, and planned changes.
Map legal, agreement, and consultation requirements for the proposed policy.
Choose programme options, eligibility principles, and proposed exception routes.
Draft policy wording, procedures, and employee guidance.

loop.input: Approved design choices, source policies, reviewed requirements, and controlled templates.
loop.output: Policy, procedure, and guidance drafts with source references and unresolved requirements.
loop.check: Validate required sections and parameter consistency; legal and HR reviewers verify obligations and substantive wording.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per document; conflicting requirements return to the legal adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: New policy wording needs synthesis across free-text agreements and chosen principles; templates only supply structure.

steps.what: Test draft procedures with recruitment, payroll, and employee-relations owners.
Consult or negotiate with employee representatives where required.
Approve final policy, implementation conditions, and effective date.
Publish approved policy and distribute implementation instructions.

tasks.design: Use the {DOCS} and {CLM} as controlled sources, with policy parameters, requirements, versions, and approvals recorded in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded loop drafts from reviewed requirements, deterministic checks compare dates and eligibility parameters, and approved publication creates implementation tasks in the {PROJECT} and notices through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy drafting crossed fragmented agreements and operational practices. Generic document automation could not resolve legal interpretation or policy tradeoffs.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled templates and approval routing already exist. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of consistency checks, while bounded drafting reduces repetitive writing.
tasks.still_hard: National rules, collective agreements, and programme interactions vary. Consultation, negotiation, legal interpretation, and implementation across several HR systems remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing defensible policy tradeoffs, negotiating acceptable terms, and anticipating how rules affect employees in practice.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends more of the week testing policy effects and consulting operational owners. Policy approval and changes to employee entitlements retain their existing decision rights.

reach.task: Plan consultation and negotiation for policy changes.
reach.learn: Learn the distinctions between information, consultation, consent, and collective bargaining.

reach.task: Prepare manager training for a new policy.
reach.learn: Learn scenario-based guidance, comprehension checks, and how to support consistent application.

reach.task: Translate approved compensation rules into payroll requirements.
reach.learn: Learn effective dating, retroactive corrections, and validation of eligibility parameters.

evidence.claim: Version control, parameter checks, and approved publication can use deterministic software; text drafting requires review.
GDPR Article 22 matters when implementation would make solely automated significant employee decisions.
The AI Act identifies specified recruitment and employment uses as high-risk; policy drafting alone does not establish that classification.
AI Act Article 26 includes worker-information duties for relevant high-risk workplace deployments.
Dutch national rules contain consent provisions relevant to specified HR policy and system changes.

assumptions: A reward manager leads compensation and benefits policy and contributes to broader HR policy with the relevant owners.
The estimate covers one policy family and reusable drafting infrastructure.
Templates, approved clauses, and structured programme parameters exist or are prepared first.
The proposed publication workflow does not change payroll, selection rules, or employee entitlements automatically.
EU GDPR and AI Act requirements apply; national rules determine consultation and employment-law requirements.
Build ranges cover active working days; bargaining or formal consent can extend elapsed delivery time.
unknowns: Which countries and collective agreements the policy covers.
Which policy sources are current and authoritative.
Who holds final approval authority for each policy family.
Whether employee representatives must consent or be consulted.
Whether publication and implementation systems expose suitable permissions and interfaces.
Whether operational owners can supply representative test scenarios.
research_questions: Which cross-document checks can detect contradictory eligibility rules and effective dates?
How well do generated guidance drafts preserve exceptions and employee rights?
What scenario set best exposes unintended effects before policy approval?
new_work: Review wording against approved requirements and agreements.
Maintain source versions, clause templates, and programme parameters.
Resolve contradictory rules and undocumented exceptions.
Verify publication, effective dates, and implementation handoffs.

role.altitude: The role moves toward job design, reward choices, service improvement, and employee consultation. Administrative preparation shrinks; legal accountability and approval authority remain explicit.
reach: Job evaluation and vacancy design with compensation specialists and HR specialists.
Service analysis and fair access with HR specialists and equal opportunity representatives.
Consultation and implementation with labor relations specialists and payroll staff.
skills_to_grow: Scenario modelling and interpretation of workforce statistics.
Data minimisation and intended-use assessment under EU law.
role.ambitious_version: Build a recurring reward-design service that connects role architecture, benefit access, and policy impact previews. With explicit delegated limits, the manager can approve small service pilots while significant policy and employee decisions retain designated human approval.
